posts.title: [MOC] Spindlejack rider
Lego Blockly: Graphical Common Programming Environment Web App (Using Intuitive Blockly) for All Lego Robotic Platforms.
posts.text: I was searching on bricklink to buy an RCX USB Tower and Powered Up Remote handset few weeks ago and found an Interface A not too expensive in B-C Canada. I just finished my ESP32 setup using @Toastie's configuration mostly. I installed a 8-Led board even if it's not really necessary but it's a nice addition for testing without Int.A. However, I do not plan to remove the ESP32 from the Int.A anytime soon :-) I used a 30-pin ESP-WROOM-32 devkit-1. Because the GPIO's aligns well with the Int.A IDC receptacle (As suggested by @Toastie setup). I didn't have IDC Connectors so I used some PCB 2.54 mm Header female pins. I glued 3 pins header for the top row pin 1, 3, 5 needed for 3.3v and gnd. I use a buck-boost DC-DC converter TPS63802 to use the 3.7v from the Int.A always-ON port to power 5V to the ESP32. Final setup: Only main power to the Int.A is required, I'm using BlueTooth to connect to Lego blockly (BT Virtual Com Port) so no need for data cable to computer.

posts.title: LEGO The Legend of Zelda - Discussion and Speculation
posts.text: Well BotW Link might look odd next to Wind Waker Link or Echoes of Wisdom Zelda but Lego and especially minifigures are a style of their own so Lego BotW link with Lego Echoes of Wisdom Zelda wouldn't look as inconsistent. Not to say that the games don't have their own styles that can vary wildly in their artistic approaches to characters, creatures and more but when turning any source material into a traditional minifig playtheme (especially when using standard minifig faces rather than specifically moulded heads or strange eyed face prints) They become as much a part of that style as they are the style of the source material. I prefer standard faces over moulded head in most cases but even with them the lego style is still as much a part of them as their orgins. You can put figs from all different themes together and they still mesh, even use print's form differen themes together to make interesting end results. Yes of course there will still be some juxtapostion but at the end of day that’s more interesting the homogeneity. Though it's the OoT theme (with the one BotW set that was also an OoT set) at the moment so I'm sure they could make whole playset waves off of one game and so no style clash would be risked.

posts.title: LEGO The Legend of Zelda - Discussion and Speculation
posts.text: I sort of feel like part of the challenge with expanding The Legend of Zelda to a full theme is that compared to many other licensed themes, Zelda games have a variety of visual styles that don't necessarily mesh with each other, making sets based on different games not complement each other quite as well. Like, Star Wars has sets based on multiple movies, shows, etc., but outside of the brief flirtation with a less traditional style for Clone Wars minifigures, you can put Star Wars characters and ships from any movie or show together without them clashing too much. Same with Mario—most modern Mario games have enough visual similarity that you could pair sets or characters based on any game from the past two decades without them looking too out of place. Zelda is a bit more stylistically siloed—apart from the Smash Bros. crossovers that deliberately pair Toon Link from the Wind Waker-era games with versions of Link from Twilight Princess, Skyward Sword, or Breath of the Wild, you rarely see games with different styles juxtaposed. That's less of an issue for adult-targeted display sets than it is for a full retail theme, where one of the main benefits is encouraging buyers to buy multiple sets that complement each other (as well as, for Lego, being able to reuse figures between multiple sets). That's probably not a totally insurmountable issue, but it does sort of add a wrinkle to the usual benefits of a full, ongoing play theme.

posts.title: So, what Do people want?
posts.text: Yes, there are excellent builders out there who share instructions and tutorials, but everyone has their own creative flair so trying to match exactly never feels as satisfying. Or can even give you a bad feeling. for not getting the exact same look and feel. Creating is a wonderful thing and everyone should give it a go! I love to build in a hybrid style of simple but greebled. Good chunky builds that people feel they can achieve, but with a little extra detail (like a few parts on a 2x2 plate instead of a printed/stickered tile). Some SNOT where offical sets would stack parts. I love the work of some of the well-known builders and my friends, but I have my style and it is not the same as anyone else.

Many an afternoon was spent building only for the structure to fail in a shower of plastic (and mostly muted swearing when I passed the age of 18) my mother knew I had some new project when there was a lot of crash noises and curses! I do have a good mechanical aptitude (got tested for a job once) but I have also been building and MOC-ing since I was a tot with Duplo, so it is a chicken/egg situation. My main advice to anyone wanting to get into MOC building is: Failure is not bad and chasing someone else's style is setting yourself up for disappointment.

posts.title: Cannon Cove, Lego 6266: A Fresh Review
posts.text: In the decades following Lego's release of the original pirate wave of 1989, building techniques have evolved. Color palette and piece inventory has evolved. Designs have become significantly more elaborate. And it would appear, for the most part, that these changes have been welcomed by the vast majority of consumers. But what about those of us who are overly nostalgic (read: "stuck in the past") about vintage sets? What venue do you have if you are more inclined toward the vintage "play sets" more than the modern "display sets?" If that description resonates with you, then this "Fresh Review" series* is for you! The purpose of this series is to bring a fresh look to older, vintage sets. Specifically their ability to be adapted and reimagined into other (albeit similar) sets. Since the history of vintage Lego Pirates is readily available to all of us, and really cannot be recreated or improved upon, these posts will focus on my own impressions and solicit similar impressions from those of you who read and feel inclined to comment. This post will focus on 1993's Cannon Cove. When this set was first released I was actually not entirely thrilled with its design. I absolutely loved the introduction of the red coats the year prior, and by the time Cannon Cove was release I had Bounty Boat and the Imperial Flagship. So I had a pretty solid contingent of redcoats on hand to face off against both the pirates and the blue coats. Still, I felt this was an awkward design, and even as a kid I wished they had made the green baseplate printed or at a minimum, yellow so it would match the "sand" from earlier pirate lego sets. To me the pirate sets were so "exotic" and the plain green baseplate felt too "classic." Many years later I would get around to addressing that as you will see later in this post. And ultimately, I felt this set, as a redcoat version of Sabre Island, was one of the better ways for me to expand upon my imperial sets. So when I had the money to get it I did exactly that. And yeah, I was underwhelmed even back then. I loved the rock piece, and the new prickly looking bush piece. But I felt the set should have come with one of those classic Lego palm trees, and as mentioned, the printed baseplate. I also felt the rowboat should have been brown and include a pirate flag. Even a couple years ago this set wasn't on my list of "must haves" when I began collecting vintage pirate sets and started building a world for them. But eventually I came around and I am glad I did. So let's take a look, shall we? Here's the actual structure. What I like about it now that I didn't appreciate as a kid is that it's actually more tactically sound as a low-profile fortified artillery position. Naturally as a kid this wasn't a priority to me and even as an adult I suppose it isn't. But after years in the military and looking at actual forts from the 1600s-early 1800s I have a much greater appreciation for what they were going for here. And of course, it came with a pirate: The boat didn't come with a pirate flag or imperial flag and I felt that was a miss (still do). And as stated, I felt if this was the pirate's boat it should have been brown. So I guess we'll just have to conclude this scurvy dog just busted out of the clink and is commandeering this imperial craft to make his escape. Missing from my set is a modified 1x1 plate and a short string that enables you to tie the boat up. They could have done away with that and included a palm tree if you ask me. Back view: As was the case with pretty much all of these vintage sets, the details are sparse. You get the cannon and some clips for a couple extra weapons. The prison built into the back of the rock is pretty cool too. But if today's detailed MOCs and UCS sets are your thing, this one will probably leave you a bit disappointed. As I mentioned, I am not a fan of the green baseplate. Both the color and the dimensions make it a little...off. And since I have pretty much zero aversion to modi

posts.title: [MOC] Lego Future Warfare Series: Episode 10 - Advance Projects Shooting Range
posts.text: Hi comrades, I’ve been busy creating new MOCs lately, and today I’m sharing a few of them, continuing my latest series. New prototypes have arrived at the firing range; the modernization of the Plighian army continues, new challenges lie on the horizon—and *si vis pacem, para bellum*. Lego ATRAHAD All Terrain Recon Attack Heavy Aracno Drone. The ATRAHAD is a ground-based drone derived from the ATVRAAD. Unlike the latter—with which it shares its characteristic shape—this drone is equipped with a comprehensive and destructive weapons suite, capable of engaging targets at any range and across a wide spectrum of types. Its armament includes a minigun with an internal magazine, a grenade launcher, and an automatic rifle. Furthermore, it features an array of sensors and protective systems, along with a slender, tapered upper body designed to keep its profile as low as possible. Unlike the ATVRAAD, this drone cannot traverse vertical surfaces, partly due to its weight. Lego Advance Projects: "Wingman" Suit. The "Wingman" heavy exoskeleton is an extremely advanced prototype of an exoskeletal suit, featuring armored protection and sophisticated combat and mobility capabilities. The operator can navigate the battlefield in three dimensions; the suit allows for free movement through the air, enabling aerial assaults on enemies, thanks to propeller engines powered by state-of-the-art solid-state batteries that provide one hour of flight time. During flight, the operator controls the wings and their surfaces via interfaces built into the suit's gloves. While the suit can reach an altitude of 200 meters, its wingspan renders it unsuitable for use in wooded or forested areas. The exoskeleton can also be operated without the wings and engines, making it useful for direct ground assaults or for moving heavy loads.

posts.title: BrickCode Studio NQC and NXC IDE for Apple Silicon and Linux
posts.text: Hi Copernicon, Thank you for the detailed feedback, it was really useful! I found the cause of the bug. Your nqc only treats a port as USB when the name starts with “usb”, so a path like /dev/usb/legousbtower0 is taken as a serial tower and fails. That is why nqc -Susb worked for you on Mint. The next version (2.0.2) sets the tower port to usb on Linux. I also added your suggestions: The target menu now shows the firmware file next to each name, for example RCX2 (firm0328.lgo). The README links to the firmware files and explains which one goes with which target. There is a Test tools button that checks that nqc and nbc are found, and a Test brick button that asks the brick for its version (and for its battery on the NXT) to confirm the USB link works. The README also has a short troubleshooting section for USB permissions. You don’t need a GitHub account or coding knowledge to help. Testing and reporting what breaks, as you did, is already a big contribution. If you have time, I would love for you to try 2.0.2 on Linux Mint once it is out, and I’m looking forward to your Mint setup steps. Thanks again!

posts.title: Marvel Superheroes 2026 - Rumors & Discussion
posts.text: Wanda and Pietro joined Hydra due to a feeling of powerlessness wanting personal revenge directed at Stark solely because his name was on the missile. I disagree with the other commentor remarking they are chaotic evil at any stage in Phase 1-3, they are misguided wanting revenge and that blinds them to the damage they are causing to others. They set off chain reactions that cause consequences but the first true exposure to consequences for their actions they see is Ultron and his desire to destroy humanity which makes them instantly want to switch sides. I like Wanda pre-Endgame her arc is from misguided villain to hero despite constantly losing. The path to redemption is paved with alienation and loss. It's beautifully tragic. That said, the point of AoU is that every other step in the process of the missile reaching them is ignored so that they can join Hydra (Nazi's), due to a desire for power they feel they lost, to kill their way to Tony Stark. As covered by Rocket's remarks, their loss shouldn’t be an excuse to get others killed. They are supposed to be scared children, radicalised and misled who eventually realise the extent of what they've created and trying to rectify that mistake. Wanda expands on Tony's trauma by altering his brain to give him a vision that reignites past trauma from Avengers/Iron Man 3, resulting in the creation of Ultron. AoU is about Wanda's redemption including killing the version of Tony Stark she created, Ultron, who represents everything they believed Tony Stark to be; arrogant, narcissistic, manipulator with zero regard for human life who is using his robots to enslave. Tony snapping at Bucky is viewed as a bad thing he does, an emotional outburst, that nearly gets him and others killed and splits the Avengers. Pietro's characterisation is one of the misguided kid who is worried for himself and his sister ultimately paying the ultimate price proving that he was just led astray by his trauma and could have easily been a great hero. Wanda was responsible in the creation of Ultron, so Pietro's death is also her punishment for her decisions as she is more directly involved in weakening the Avengers throughout the movie and as such is more crucial to the defeat of the primary Ultron and his plan at the end of the movie. It's no coincidence that Ultron is primarily born from the trauma of both Wanda and Tony. Howard Stark was the one who created Stark Industries, do we need to consider that? Tony Stark's life was influenced by his parents being killed by the Winter Soldier, do we need to consider that? Bucky only became the Winter Soldier because of Steve saving him from a prison camp and going on a mission with him, do we need to consider that? Steve only became a Super Soldier because of a US program born from fear of Hydra, do we need to consider that? Hydra only gathered powered thanks to the Cosmic Cube/Infinity Stone, do we need to consider that? The Cosmic Cube was retrieved by Red Skull, do we need to consider that? You can go down this sort of blame game forever. At every step characters had a choice and the movie and prequel comic acknowledges it was Wanda & Pietro's decision to go after personal revenge by joining Hydra. Personally I think Clint sacrificing himself because of him wanting to save his family and to give Natasha to get a chance at a normal life, allowing her to accept retiring to be the aunt for his family would have hit harder. That's the fault of Infinity War/Endgame being horrifically written, made by people who disliked well written female characters, like Gamora and Natasha, who had become fan favourites. The writers were embarrassed that the development of Gamora and Natasha put to shame their own handling of female characters such as how Natasha, Sharon Carter and other female characters where handled in Winter Soldier and Civil War - go back and watch those now and you'll see. You can even look toward how Sue Storm is apparently being handled as a prize, an object

Quite the opposite. :D I would imagine the version of star lord in the movies was literally based on Han to some extent. In most of the comics up to around that point, he's a pretty straight-laced military man. It's kind of fun going back to the pre-MCU cartoons and he shows up with the same voice actor as Halo's Master Chief. They really are just going for puns or seemingly entirely random mashups. Iron-3PO and War2-D2 are the biggest offenders to me (aside from Captain Alderaan if she really ends up being based on captain carter) because C-3PO is a character that's just fundamentally uncool, so I can't imagine the C-3PO/Iron Man figure being all that interesting. The droids are pretty tough to accurately ascribe major marvel characters to, but with the set only having 5 figures... just don't use the droids. Could have been Luke Spiderwalker, Solo-Lord, Grootbacca (Solo-lord's limited-speech, strong companion who's smarter than he appears), Invisileia (I was struggling to find a Leia match at first but they both use the force, they're both diplomats -at least in more modern stories for Sue- and Leia does a fair bit of sneaking around in ANH), and Vadoom (obviously) or something.
